Закоммиченный вывод, который никто не пересобрал

Вы узнаете

Почему seal --verify обязан сравнивать закоммиченный сгенерированный файл с его генератором, а не с записанным хешем.

Печать хранит хеши четырёх сгенерированных бэкендов, но на стенде seal --verify ни разу не открывал сгенерированные файлы, закоммиченные рядом со спекой: digest_cache.rs, обрезанный до 200 байт, проходил проверку с пятью строками MATCH. gen_file_check.t27 добавляет правило. Закоммиченный файл проходит, если его нет или он равен тому, что выдаёт его генератор, а файл, который нельзя прочитать или который не пишет ни один генератор, не проходит. verify_passes требует, чтобы записанные хеши совпали и все четыре файла прошли. Сравнение идёт с генератором, потому что из 124 закоммиченных файлов 61 даёт хеш, записанный в печати, а 63 нет.

Попробовать

Начните с обрезанного файла Rust и прочитайте вердикт. Потом сделайте этот файл отсутствующим, а затем осиротевшим.

Открыть интерактивный урок →

A seal records hashes, and on the lab seal --verify never opened the generated files committed beside a spec. Set the state of each file and see whether the rule passes.

specs/verified/gen_file_check.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/verified/gen_file_check.t27 -- what `t27c seal --verify` owes the committed gen file of a
; spec: when one exists, its bytes are what the spec's generator emits today, or the verify fails.
; gHashTag/t27#10457, follow-up A. Measured on the Railway lab with t27c 0.5.2 built from master
; 982894c96, 2026-10-18.
; --
; What already exists and is NOT restated here:
; - specs/verified/seal_check.t27 says how a seal is checked from its recorded inputs. That check
;   regenerates every backend in memory and compares the recorded gen_hash_* with the fresh
;   output. It never opens a file under gen/ or bootstrap/gen/. This file is that missing read.
; - specs/verified/seal_write.t27 (#10458) says what one seal write must guarantee. This file is
;   about the generated files committed next to the seals, which no seal write produces.
; - .github/workflows/spec-guards.yml regenerates six named committed gen files and runs
;   `git diff --exit-code`. The rule here covers every committed gen file, not only those six.
; --
; The gap, as found on the lab:
; - bootstrap/gen/rust/verified/digest_cache.rs truncated to its first 200 bytes: `t27c seal
;   specs/verified/digest_cache.t27 --verify` printed five MATCH lines, "all hashes MATCH", exit 0.
; - one hand-written fn appended to bootstrap/gen/rust/verified/bench_boards.rs: "all hashes
;   MATCH", exit 0. That file is compiled into t27c itself (bootstrap/src/main.rs #[path]).
; --
; Why the comparison is against the generator, not against the recorded gen_hash_*:
; the first version of this rule (issue comment 6250250375) said the committed file must hash to
; the recorded gen_hash_*. That is right only for a spec with no `use`. `seal` hashes the
; generation of the unresolved source; `t27c gen-rust` and `t27c gen-c`, which write the committed
; files, resolve `use` first. Measured:
;   digest_cache   (no use)  file cd6233d7..  gen-rust cd6233d7..  seal gen_hash_rust cd6233d7..
;   bench_boards   (3 use)   file 80cfd58e..  gen-rust 80cfd58e..  seal gen_hash_rust adc58ade..
;   die_binding    (2 use)   file 79025f3a..  gen-rust 79025f3a..  seal gen_hash_rust f57ce0a9..
;   claw/gates     (1 use)   file acf1850e..  gen-c    acf1850e..  seal gen_hash_c    31f55358..
; claw/gates.c is one of the six files spec-guards proves fresh, and all four seals verify. Over the
; tree, 61 of the 124 committed files under gen/ and bootstrap/gen/ hash to some value a seal
; records, and 63 do not. The recorded-hash rule would refuse untouched files like these; the
; generator rule refuses only the truncated and the hand-edited one.
; --
; The rule, per backend of one spec:
; - The committed gen files of specs/<rel>.t27 are bootstrap/gen/rust/<rel>.rs, gen/rust/<rel>.rs,
;   gen/c/<rel>.c, gen/verilog/<rel>.v and gen/json/<rel>.json. gen/json has no gen_hash_* field
;   in any seal, so only the generator rule can check it.
; - No such file: nothing to check. Most specs have none, and the seal still certifies the
;   regenerated output.
; - The file exists: it must hash to what `t27c gen-<backend> <spec>` emits today. That is the
;   generation of the `use`-resolved source, or of the unresolved source when the resolved one does
;   not compile (gen-rust's fallback, which it announces with a note).
; - The file exists but cannot be read, or the backend no longer generates anything for the spec:
;   fail closed. A file that no generator emits cannot be generated output.
; - `--verify` passes only when the recorded hashes match AND every committed gen file passes.
;   This check adds to the seal check; it replaces none of it.
; Hashes are stand-ins: the first 32 bits of the measured sha256, compared whole.
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module VerifiedGenFileCheck;

/// gen_file_check() answers.
pub const GEN_OK : u8 = 0;
pub const GEN_ABSENT : u8 = 1;
pub const GEN_DRIFT : u8 = 2;
pub const GEN_UNREADABLE : u8 = 3;
pub const GEN_ORPHAN : u8 = 4;

/// What `t27c gen-<backend> <spec>` emits: the generation of the `use`-resolved source, unless
/// that does not compile and the generator falls back to the unresolved one. For a spec with no
/// `use` the two are the same bytes.
pub fn producer_hash(resolved_compiles: bool, unresolved: u64, resolved: u64) -> u64 {
    if (resolved_compiles) { return resolved; }
    return unresolved;
}

/// One committed gen file against its generator. exists covers every home listed above;
/// readable says its bytes could be read; producer_ok says the backend generated anything today.
pub fn gen_file_check(exists: bool, readable: bool, file_hash: u64, producer_ok: bool, producer: u64) -> u8 {
    if (exists == false) { return GEN_ABSENT; }
    if (readable == false) { return GEN_UNREADABLE; }
    if (producer_ok == false) { return GEN_ORPHAN; }
    if (file_hash == producer) { return GEN_OK; }
    return GEN_DRIFT;
}

/// The rule as first proposed: the file against the recorded gen_hash_*. Kept as the reference
/// that false-alarms on every untouched file of a spec with `use`.
pub fn gen_file_check_recorded(exists: bool, file_hash: u64, recorded: u64) -> u8 {
    if (exists == false) { return GEN_ABSENT; }
    if (file_hash == recorded) { return GEN_OK; }
    return GEN_DRIFT;
}

/// `seal --verify` today: the committed file is never opened. The unsafe reference.
pub fn gen_file_check_today(exists: bool, readable: bool, file_hash: u64, producer_ok: bool, producer: u64) -> u8 {
    return GEN_OK;
}

/// A committed file passes when it is absent or equal to its generator's output.
pub fn gen_file_passes(code: u8) -> bool {
    if (code == GEN_OK) { return true; }
    return code == GEN_ABSENT;
}

/// The verdict of `seal --verify` over the recorded hashes and the four backends' committed files
/// (rust covers both rust homes).
pub fn verify_passes(seal_all_match: bool, rust: u8, c: u8, verilog: u8, json: u8) -> bool {
    if (seal_all_match == false) { return false; }
    if (gen_file_passes(rust) == false) { return false; }
    if (gen_file_passes(c) == false) { return false; }
    if (gen_file_passes(verilog) == false) { return false; }
    return gen_file_passes(json);
}

/// `seal --verify` today: the recorded hashes decide alone.
pub fn verify_passes_today(seal_all_match: bool, rust: u8, c: u8, verilog: u8, json: u8) -> bool {
    return seal_all_match;
}

test an_untouched_file_of_a_spec_without_use_passes {
    // digest_cache: the file, gen-rust and the seal all say cd6233d7..
    var producer : u64 = producer_hash(true, 0xcd6233d7, 0xcd6233d7);
    assert producer == 0xcd6233d7;
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0xcd6233d7, true, producer) == 0;
    assert verify_passes(true, gen_file_check(true, true, 0xcd6233d7, true, producer), GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) == true;
}

test the_lab_truncation_fails_the_verify {
    // digest_cache.rs cut to 200 bytes hashes to 675400d8..; today's verify said all hashes MATCH
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0x675400d8, true, 0xcd6233d7) == 2;
    assert verify_passes(true, GEN_DRIFT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) == false;
}

test the_lab_hand_edit_fails_the_verify {
    // bench_boards.rs with one appended fn hashes to ea48aa9b..; gen-rust emits 80cfd58e..
    var producer : u64 = producer_hash(true, 0xadc58ade, 0x80cfd58e);
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0xea48aa9b, true, producer) == 2;
}

test an_untouched_file_of_a_spec_with_use_passes {
    // bench_boards and die_binding (gen-rust) and claw/gates (gen-c): the file is the resolved
    // generation, which the seal does not record
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0x80cfd58e, true, producer_hash(true, 0xadc58ade, 0x80cfd58e)) == 0;
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0x79025f3a, true, producer_hash(true, 0xf57ce0a9, 0x79025f3a)) == 0;
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0xacf1850e, true, producer_hash(true, 0x31f55358, 0xacf1850e)) == 0;
}

test negative_control_the_recorded_hash_refuses_untouched_files {
    // the rule as first proposed calls all three untouched files drift; it would turn
    // `seal --verify` red on files nobody edited
    assert gen_file_check_recorded(true, 0x80cfd58e, 0xadc58ade) == GEN_DRIFT;
    assert gen_file_check_recorded(true, 0x79025f3a, 0xf57ce0a9) == GEN_DRIFT;
    assert gen_file_check_recorded(true, 0xacf1850e, 0x31f55358) == GEN_DRIFT;
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0x80cfd58e, true, 0x80cfd58e) != gen_file_check_recorded(true, 0x80cfd58e, 0xadc58ade);
    // where the spec has no `use`, the two rules agree
    assert gen_file_check_recorded(true, 0xcd6233d7, 0xcd6233d7) == gen_file_check(true, true, 0xcd6233d7, true, 0xcd6233d7);
}

test negative_control_today_passes_the_truncation {
    // today's verify never reads the file. Weaken the rule to today's and these lines fail.
    assert gen_file_check_today(true, true, 0x675400d8, true, 0xcd6233d7) == GEN_OK;
    assert verify_passes_today(true, GEN_DRIFT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) == true;
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0x675400d8, true, 0xcd6233d7) != gen_file_check_today(true, true, 0x675400d8, true, 0xcd6233d7);
    assert verify_passes(true, GEN_DRIFT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) != verify_passes_today(true, GEN_DRIFT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT);
}

test an_absent_file_is_not_drift {
    // a spec with no committed gen file verifies on its recorded hashes alone
    assert gen_file_check(false, false, 0, true, 0xcd6233d7) == 1;
    assert gen_file_passes(GEN_ABSENT) == true;
    assert verify_passes(true, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) == true;
}

test an_unreadable_file_fails_closed {
    assert gen_file_check(true, false, 0, true, 0xcd6233d7) == 3;
    assert gen_file_passes(GEN_UNREADABLE) == false;
}

test a_file_its_backend_no_longer_generates_fails {
    // the spec stopped lowering to this backend; the committed file is left over, not generated
    assert gen_file_check(true, true, 0xcd6233d7, false, 0) == 4;
    assert gen_file_passes(GEN_ORPHAN) == false;
}

test the_generator_falls_back_to_the_unresolved_source {
    // gen-rust: a spliced source that does not compile is dropped, with a note
    assert producer_hash(false, 0xadc58ade, 0x80cfd58e) == 0xadc58ade;
    assert producer_hash(true, 0xadc58ade, 0x80cfd58e) == 0x80cfd58e;
}

test one_drifting_backend_fails_the_verify {
    // any of the four homes is enough; the c file of a spec whose rust file is fine
    assert verify_passes(true, GEN_OK, GEN_DRIFT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) == false;
    assert verify_passes(true, GEN_OK, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ORPHAN) == false;
    assert verify_passes(true, GEN_OK, GEN_OK, GEN_OK, GEN_OK) == true;
}

test negative_control_the_file_check_does_not_replace_the_seal_check {
    // fresh committed files do not rescue a seal whose recorded hashes differ
    assert verify_passes(false, GEN_OK, GEN_OK, GEN_OK, GEN_OK) == false;
    assert verify_passes(false, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT, GEN_ABSENT) == false;
}
